quote: We're a certified solar installer for Tesla.
stewart_read: Rep used the standard solar/Tesla intro on a lead that actually requested Powerwall only, triggering immediate pushback.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may not have had the lead notes loaded yet at second 0, making this a system-lag issue rather than a script error.
coaching_implication: Confirm lead intent (solar vs. battery-only) before applying the solar-installer framing, or use a product-neutral opener until notes load.

quote: Yeah. It looks like you were looking into the Powerwall, the test Powerwall. Okay.
stewart_read: Rep transparently corrects course once the actual lead detail loads, recovering credibility instead of arguing the original frame.
coaching_implication: This recovery move is a good model — name it as a positive example of admit-and-recover rather than dodge or fabricate.

quote: The only requirement to qualify is that you have a credit score of 6 50 or higher.
stewart_read: Rep states 650 as the threshold, matching the schema's noted drift from the documented 670 standard.
coaching_implication: Flag for reconciliation with Kenny on which threshold is current policy; this is a floor-wide drift, not isolated to this rep.

stewart_read: Rep captures the $300 bill and immediately files it with a flat acknowledgment, no reflection or flip.
coaching_implication: Should have reflected the number back ('$300 a month is a lot going straight to Dominion') to build urgency before moving to scheduling.

quote: An alternate day of the week. I'm on a hybrid schedule,
stewart_read: Customer volunteers a scheduling constraint cooperatively; rep adapts by offering Friday/tomorrow slots without friction.
coaching_implication: No coaching gap here — this is a clean scheduling adaptation, worth noting as competent handling.

quote: There's too many Okay. Links that are getting crazy.
stewart_read: Customer signals text-link fatigue/scam wariness right at the bill-collection ask; rep pivots to email without addressing the underlying suspicion.
alternative_hypothesis: The pivot to email could itself be read as the correct accommodation rather than a missed trust moment, since customer's actual need (avoid texts) was met.
coaching_implication: Acknowledge the scam-fatigue comment directly ('totally get it, lot of shady texts out there') before pivoting channels — closes the trust gap instead of just routing around it.

quote: I'll send you that text. And then if you could get that or sorry. Email.
stewart_read: Rep verbally stumbles between text and email mid-sentence right after the customer explicitly rejected text, a small but avoidable confusion that could re-trigger the trust concern.
alternative_hypothesis: Simple verbal slip under call pace, not a substantive process error since he corrects to email in the same breath.
coaching_implication: Slow down on the channel confirmation right after a customer states a channel preference — the slip is minor but timing matters when trust was just flagged.
